instruction: I'm listening to music in VLC while reading lecture notes. Sometimes I need to stop the music completely when taking a phone call. Could you set up a global keyboard shortcut to stop playback in VLC? This way I can quickly stop the music from any application without having to switch windows.

parameters.window_name: lecture.pdf — 6.006 Introduction to Algorithms, Lecture 2: Data Structures

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires setting up a global keyboard shortcut for VLC's stop function, allowing control without window switching. The evaluator checks the global-key-stop setting in VLC's config file. Expected value is 1 (set). Similar complexity to original task - both require changing VLC global hotkey settings for background control.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads VLC config file from OS-specific path (vlc.py:35-61)
Metric includes robust validation logic via is_valid_keyboard_shortcut function (metrics/vlc.py:7-66)
Validation function uses multiple regex patterns to match valid keyboard shortcuts (Ctrl+S, Alt-F4, F1, etc.)
Rejects common invalid values ('invalid', 'test', 'none', etc.) effectively
Complete coverage: Instruction requires setting global shortcut, evaluator verifies 'global-key-stop' is set with valid shortcut value
Postconfig appropriately kills and relaunches VLC to ensure config is written to disk
Binary expected value (1=valid shortcut set, 0=not set) is semantically correct - instruction doesn't specify which shortcut to use
Data flow is correct: getter extracts config file -> metric validates shortcut value -> comparison with expected
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: Validation regex might not catch all edge cases of VLC's internal shortcut formats, but covers common cases well
Consider adding logging for which specific shortcut value was found during validation for debugging purposes
